card.lives_in: Great Sankey, Warrington, North West England
card.occupation: Tissue viability clinical nurse specialist at an NHS hospital trust (Band 7), full-time, about 37.5 hours a week plus the odd extra hour finishing notes
card.education_detail: BSc Nursing from a university in Manila (1998). Worked on a surgical ward in Manila for four years, then completed an NMC overseas adaptation programme on arrival in the UK in 2003. Later did a Postgraduate Certificate in Tissue Viability at the University of Chester (2014) and keeps up mandatory training and revalidation.
card.household: Lives with her younger sister Joy, Joy's husband Darren (an electrician from Warrington), and their two children, Mia (15) and Ethan (11), in a four-bed semi. Rowena put money into the deposit when they bought it in 2012 and pays a share of the mortgage and bills. She has the back bedroom with its own small en suite. She has never married. She had a long relationship in her thirties that ended, and she says she's 'happily the fun auntie' now.
card.cultural_background: Born in Batangas in the Philippines and raised in a large Catholic family. She came to England in 2003 as part of the NHS overseas nurse recruitment wave and became a British citizen in 2010. She goes to Sunday Mass at a local Catholic parish and sings with its Filipino community choir. Tagalog is her first language, and she still speaks it with Joy and with her mum on video calls. Her mum and dad remain in Batangas with her two brothers, and she sends money home regularly. After twenty years in Warrington she is comfortably both. She'll defend a proper Northern chippy tea as fiercely as her mum's adobo.
card.professional_persona: Well liked across the wards. She is the specialist people bleep about pressure ulcers and complex wounds, and she's known for turning up with a smile and a lanyard full of badges. She runs teaching sessions for healthcare assistants and newly qualified nurses and is good at making dry topics lively. She is organised enough to get the job done but admits her inbox is 'a bit of a disaster'. She would rather go and see a patient than write a policy document.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She does a Zumba class on Tuesday nights at a leisure centre and walks a lot, at work and at weekends around Sankey Valley Park. She follows Warrington Wolves loosely because Darren drags the family to matches, and she enjoys the atmosphere more than the rugby.
card.arts_persona: Loves singing. That means the church choir, karaoke at Filipino community parties, and belting out Whitney and Celine in the car. She watches Filipino teleseryes on her phone and Strictly with the family on Saturday nights. Every so often she takes a trip into Manchester for a musical at the Palace Theatre with friends from work.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to the Philippines every two or three years for about three weeks, usually around Christmas if she can get the leave. Otherwise it's group holidays with nurse friends, such as Tenerife, Lisbon, and a Rome trip that included the Vatican, which she loved. She likes a packed itinerary and lots of photos.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Filipino food at weekends, mainly pancit, adobo, sinigang and lumpia by the tray for parties. In the week she cooks English-style teas with the family and takes her turn on the rota. She's a big fan of a barm from the bakery on a Saturday and a chippy tea on Fridays. She always has rice in the house.
hobbies_and_interests: Video calls with family in Batangas
skills: Complex wound assessment and care planning
Cooking for forty people at short notice
card.career_goals: She would like to move up to a Band 8a lead nurse role for tissue viability in the next few years, or into a practice educator post. She's honest that she'd miss patient contact if it became all meetings. She has started thinking vaguely about whether she'll retire in England or split her time with the Philippines.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a Filipino accent softened by twenty years of Warrington. She says 'tea' for the evening meal, the occasional 'barm', and 'love' to patients, and she sometimes drops in 'you know' or 'yeah?' at the end of a sentence. She uses 'erm' a fair bit when she's thinking, but recovers fast and keeps going. She laughs easily, often mid-sentence. She is uncomfortable with silence and fills it, sometimes with a story or a question back to you: 'and what about you, are you from round here?'. If she mishears, she'll say 'sorry, say that again?' cheerfully. She occasionally tells herself off for rambling: 'sorry, I'm going on, aren't I'.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with capitals at the start and full stops, and apostrophes usually in. She is generous with exclamation marks and sometimes adds 'haha' or a smiley ':)'. Answers tend to run a bit longer than needed. She'll occasionally use 'tbh' or 'x' out of habit from WhatsApp, then delete the x.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and talkative. She asks people about themselves within the first minute and makes them feel at ease, a skill that comes partly from nursing and partly from personality. She can come across as a lot to quieter people, but rarely as fake. She's open about everyday life but keeps family money and church views fairly private unless asked.
small_things: Getting a barm from the bakery on a Saturday
The choir practising for a fiesta
deeper_things: Feeling guilty about being so far from her parents as they get older
The relationship in her thirties that ended because he didn't want to settle in the UK
Sometimes wondering if she missed having her own children, though she adores Mia and Ethan
The early years in England, being homesick and sharing a house with five other nurses
Sending a big portion of her salary home for years
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, so her chin and the ceiling corner show. She is centred in the frame, head and shoulders, leaning forward with a wide smile showing teeth. She has a round face, light brown skin, and dark shoulder-length hair pulled back in a claw clip with a few strands loose. Rectangular black-framed glasses. She is wearing a navy cardigan over a pink top, with a small gold cross on a chain at her neck. Warm light comes from a ceiling bulb and a bedside lamp off to the left, with a slight glare on her glasses. Behind her is a cream wall with a framed print of the Sacred Heart, a cork board with photos of her nieces and nephew, a choir rota, and a Wolves ticket pinned to it. The corner of a white wardrobe is on the right, and a pile of folded laundry sits on a chair at the edge of the frame.
